topic.readerProblem: A founder, marketer or agency lead wants Claude to name and link their brand when buyers ask for recommendations, needs to know whether and when Claude cites sources, which Anthropic crawlers to allow, and how to check the result; a minority of readers only want to know how Claude can help their own SEO work.
topic.connection: AEOeye's full report tests Claude alongside the other major AI engines at the default free-user tier; this guide explains Claude's documented search and citation path, uses AEOeye's own crawler access study (Claude bots by site group) and audit records with their caveats, and tells the reader what to change when Claude does not name them.

assessment: The page answers one question, how to get Claude to cite and recommend a brand, by describing Claude's web search and citation behavior as Anthropic documents it (help center, API docs and crawler page, October 2026), separating the three Anthropic bots with what Anthropic says blocking each one does, and giving an ordered six-step playbook plus a repeated-prompt measurement protocol. It absorbs the 'does Claude cite sources?' answer page as the first section and keeps 'using Claude for SEO work' to one short section. It rests on Anthropic's own pages, two arXiv papers, a Vercel crawler analysis, SparkToro's consistency study and AEOeye's crawler access study (384 sites) and audit records (509 Claude answers, with their caveats). It deliberately does not claim a ranking formula, a timeline, that Brave Search definitively powers Claude (reported by TechCrunch, unconfirmed by Anthropic), or that llms.txt or schema moves Claude citations, and it drops the old pages' unverified comparisons of Claude, ChatGPT and Perplexity citation styles and their unsupported claims about what Claude is 'better' at.

sources.supports: Defines generative engine optimization, also called AEO, as the practice of improving visibility in responses generated by generative AI systems.

When Claude searches, every response includes citations; accounts on the new Claude experience have no web search toggle and Claude searches when it helps; including 'Search the web' in a prompt makes Claude search; users should cross-reference cited sources and verify important information.

Claude searches for current, changing or outside-training information (including organizations and products that might have changed) and answers directly for stable knowledge; searches can repeat within one request (simple questions typically 1 to 3, comparative or multi-entity research 10 or more); citations are always enabled and carry URL, title and up to 150 characters of cited text; results carry a page_age field; pricing of $10 per 1,000 searches plus token costs; the page does not name a search provider.

Anthropic's page (dated April 7, 2026) describes three bots: ClaudeBot (training), Claude-User (user-initiated fetches) and Claude-SearchBot (search quality) with what happens when each is disabled; bots honor robots.txt and Crawl-delay; opt-out must be done per subdomain; blocking by IP address may not work because it stops Anthropic reading robots.txt.

March 2025 TechCrunch report (syndicated on Yahoo Finance) that Anthropic added Brave Search to its subprocessor list, a developer found identical citations and a BraveSearchParams parameter, and Anthropic had not confirmed.

September 2025 preprint: 1,000 consumer ranking prompts across Claude (claude-3.5-sonnet-latest with the web_search_20250305 tool), Gemini, GPT search and Perplexity; in the U.S. software category AI search returned 72.7% earned, 26.7% brand and negligible social sources versus 45.4% earned and 43.7% brand for Google.
December 2024 analysis of Vercel's network: Claude's crawler fetched JavaScript files in 23.84% of requests but did not execute them; recommends server-side rendering for critical content.
RFC 9309 states robots.txt rules are not a form of access authorization and are rules crawlers are requested to honor.
GEO paper accepted to KDD 2024: generative engine optimization can boost visibility in generative engine responses by up to 40%, on the GEO-bench benchmark.

Full text: Cite Sources, Quotation Addition and Statistics Addition achieved 30-40% relative improvement on Position-Adjusted Word Count; keyword stuffing offered little to no improvement; main evaluation used a gpt-3.5-turbo engine and was also run on Perplexity.ai.

Published 27 January 2026: 600 volunteers, 12 prompts, 2,961 runs across ChatGPT, Claude and Google AI; under a 1-in-100 chance that ChatGPT or Google's AI repeats the same brand list, Claude slightly more consistent on lists but less likely to repeat the order; visibility percentage across many runs is a reasonable metric, ranking position is not; the author suggests asking 60-100 times.
Claude Code is an agentic coding tool that reads your codebase, edits files, runs commands and integrates with development tools.

Google warns that generating many pages with AI without adding value may violate its scaled content abuse policy and says to fact-check AI-generated content before publishing; page shows last updated 1 October 2026.
